lesson.summary: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations
points: A declaration pairs a type and name; initialization supplies a first value, and assignment changes it.
Practice int, float, double and char, with suitable printf formats.
Names are case sensitive. Do not read an uninitialized automatic local.
lesson.title: Basic Parts of C and Variable Declarations

objective: Declare float: declare resource as float, apply resource + 5.5, and print each result with %.1f. Dataset 5 starts with [-3, 0, 12, 15]. Match every stream. Use a full main function and a return statement.
hint: Declare before use. float resource = readInput(); creates the named game-port value; printf uses %.1f.
controls: Edit the C program. Run tests all streams; Step shows declarations, assignments and output. readInput() is a LogiCade game-port helper declared in logicade.h. This safe practice runtime supports a documented C subset.
